purpose: Bendamustine is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain blood cancers, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. It helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer cells in your body. Your cancer doctor has chosen this medicine as part of your treatment plan.
how_it_works: Bendamustine works by damaging the DNA inside cancer cells, which stops them from being able to grow and multiply. Think of it like putting a wrench in the machinery that cancer cells use to copy themselves. Because cancer cells divide much faster than normal cells, they are more affected by this medicine.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, tiredness, and fever. You may also notice a drop in your blood counts, which can make you more prone to infections, bruising, or feeling weak and short of breath. Some people also experience skin rashes, headache, or loss of appetite.
warnings: Because bendamustine lowers your immune system, you are at a higher risk of getting serious infections, so let your doctor know right away if you have a fever or feel unwell. It can also cause severe skin reactions in rare cases. This medicine can harm an unborn baby, so pregnancy must be avoided during treatment. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as some can interact with this drug.
typical_dosing: Bendamustine is given through an IV (a drip into your vein) at a cancer clinic or hospital. The dose and how often you receive it depends on the type of cancer being treated and your body size. It is usually given on specific days of a treatment cycle, often every 3 to 4 weeks, and your oncology team will give you a personalized schedule.
